intended_object: Take a morphism f : H → K of commutative Hopf algebras over a commutative ring R. Its kernel Hopf ideal is K·f(H⁺), the ideal of K generated by the image of the augmentation ideal H⁺ = ker ε_H. The quotient K/K·f(H⁺) = K ⊗_H R is the coordinate ring of the kernel of the induced group-scheme map Spec K → Spec H (Milne, Algebraic Groups, Prop. 4.1). This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body is `(HopfIdeal.augmentation R H).map f.hom`.

- `HopfIdeal.augmentation R H` is the kernel Hopf ideal of the counit, `kerOfSurjective (counitBialgHom R H)`, so it is H⁺ = ker ε.
- `HopfIdeal.map` is `ofSpan (f '' I)`, and `map_toIdeal` shows its underlying ideal is `Ideal.map f I`. That is the ideal of K generated by f(H⁺).

So the definition gives K·f(H⁺). This is the standard ideal: the fibre of Spec K → Spec H over the identity section is Spec(K ⊗_H H/H⁺) = Spec(K/K·f(H⁺)). The library's trivialization criterion (`kernelHopfIdeal_toIdeal_le_ker_iff`) confirms the universal property: a map φ out of K kills the ideal exactly when φ∘f equals the counit followed by the unit.

There are no degenerate-case problems. When f is surjective, the result is the augmentation ideal of K, i.e. the trivial kernel, as it should be.

The generality is right. The setting is commutative Hopf algebras over an arbitrary commutative ring R, which is the natural setting for kernels of affine group schemes. Commutativity of K is what makes the extended ideal two-sided.

Mathlib has only the predicate `Ideal.IsHopfIdeal` and quotient Hopf algebras. It has no kernel-of-a-morphism construction, so there is no counterpart.
